declared_purpose: Monitor stocks, ETFs and gold using seven alert rules, severity levels, holding-cost calculations, background scheduling and news analysis. Overnight and weekend monitoring is expressly gold-only and hourly. These are functional requirements; particular providers, request breadth and logging arrangements are implementation choices (SKILL.md:1-29, 69-88, 90-139, 175-181; README.md:1-19).

data_operations.data_scope: Configured instrument codes, names, markets, types, costs and alert thresholds; packaged values are defaults, not evidence of actual user holdings.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local monitor process memory; the configuration already resides in scripts/monitor.py.
data_operations.condition: When the monitor module is imported or executed. No separate holdings-file reader is shown.

data_operations.operation: Disclose selected instruments and retrieve current quotes
data_operations.data_scope: A batch of market-prefixed stock/ETF codes, or the fixed gold identifier hf_XAU. Receives prices, OHLC, volume, amount and timestamps. Configured holding costs and thresholds are not included in these requests.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: HTTPS hq.sinajs.cn; parsed results return to the local caller.
data_operations.condition: Each requested scan. Direct smart-mode scans use the scheduled subset; smart_mode=False uses the full WATCHLIST, including in the daemon.

data_operations.operation: Disclose instrument identifiers and retrieve historical market data
data_operations.data_scope: Market-qualified secid and requested field/window parameters; responses contain two, six or thirty daily records with eleven requested K-line fields.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: HTTPS push2his.eastmoney.com/api/qt/stock/kline/get; response data and calculations remain with the local caller.
data_operations.condition: Two-day fallback when stock/ETF quotes are missing or invalid; six-day volume lookup for configured non-gold volume checks with positive volume; thirty-day technical lookup when non-gold ma_monitor is enabled, which defaults to True.

data_operations.operation: Infer financial alert attributes and recommendations locally
data_operations.source: Configured costs and rules, retrieved prices/history, news titles and fixed correlation mappings
data_operations.data_scope: Cost-relative profit/loss percentages and target prices, daily changes, volume ratios, MA/RSI signals, estimated gaps, drawdowns, alert severity, news sentiment and rule-based advice. Gold correlation uses a fixed instrument mapping.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local process and calling function; no model-service request is implemented for the text labelled Kimi advice.
data_operations.condition: When relevant checks or analyser methods execute. RSI follows ma_monitor rather than rsi_monitor; gap and trailing-stop checks do not consult their documented switches.

data_operations.source: Triggered instrument code and alert type
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: StockAlert.alert_log in process memory; no disk persistence is shown.
data_operations.condition: Recorded while constructing alerts. Entries at least thirty minutes old are removed when _alerted_recently runs.

data_operations.data_scope: Configured instrument name, type=14 and count, normally five. Receives titles, URLs and publication times; locally derives sentiment and selects two shortened titles for the report.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: HTTPS searchapi.eastmoney.com/api/suggest/get; fetched data and report return locally.
data_operations.condition: During generate_insight after an alert, when analyser execution succeeds; also on direct helper invocation and the analyser's standalone demonstration. The symbol argument is not transmitted by this helper.

data_operations.operation: Request fund-flow data without consuming the response
data_operations.data_scope: Market-prefixed instrument code and source=sina. The method returns fixed placeholder strings or an error; generate_insight does not use its result.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: HTTPS quotes.sina.cn/cn/api/quotes.php; placeholder result stays local.
data_operations.condition: Every generate_insight execution that reaches the fund-flow call, plus direct helper invocation.

data_operations.data_scope: Instrument name in the URL query. Response HTML is unused; the returned news item is a locally constructed placeholder.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: HTTPS search.sina.com.cn; placeholder returned to the caller.
data_operations.condition: Only if this helper is invoked; no packaged monitoring-path call is shown.

data_operations.data_scope: Fixed secid=1.000001 and fields=f170, rather than user holdings. Response content is unused.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: HTTPS push2.eastmoney.com/api/qt/stock/get; a fixed placeholder returns locally.
data_operations.condition: Only if this helper is invoked; no packaged monitoring-path call is shown.

data_operations.data_scope: Supplied date or current local date, report identifier, sorting, page size fifty and columns=ALL. Returns the provider's result data without local field filtering.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: HTTP datacenter-web.eastmoney.com/api/data/v1/get; normal return to the caller.
data_operations.condition: Only if this helper is invoked; no packaged monitoring-path call is shown.

data_operations.data_scope: Supplied symbol in the code parameter. Response content is unused and the method returns a fixed readiness message.
data_operations.condition: Only if this helper is invoked; run_once instead uses StockAnalyser.

data_operations.data_scope: Instrument identity, price/change, configured cost and derived profit/loss, alert explanations and optional news analysis. The analyser demonstration prints sample news, sentiment and correlation.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: run_once caller; stdout when monitor.py or analyser.py runs directly. The daemon receives reports and logs their count; no notification recipient or sending implementation is present.
data_operations.condition: Reports are returned when alerts trigger; standalone monitor execution prints them. A normal function return does not establish remote disclosure.

data_operations.operation: Persist operational logs and conditional diagnostics
data_operations.data_scope: Timestamps, lifecycle events, scan modes/counts, alert counts and errors with tracebacks. Fallback/error prints can additionally contain instrument names, codes, prices and exception text; daemon code does not log complete alert reports.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: ~/.stock_monitor/monitor.log through FileHandler; the same events also reach stdout, which control.sh redirects into that file along with stderr.
data_operations.condition: Daemon logging is configured on module load. Redirected monitor diagnostics persist when launched through control.sh start. No in-process rotation is configured.

data_operations.operation: Store/read process metadata, read logs and delete or truncate local files
data_operations.data_scope: Daemon PID and operational log contents.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: ~/.stock_monitor/monitor.pid and monitor.log; PID/status and log output go to the invoking terminal.
data_operations.condition: start writes the PID and truncates monitor.log through > redirection. status reads the PID and last five log lines; log follows the file. stop reads the PID, terminates an existing process and removes the PID file, including stale PID files; it does not remove the log.

data_operations.operation: Make live data requests during tests
data_operations.source: test_suite.py data-fetching, alert-rule and integration tests
data_operations.data_scope: WATCHLIST instruments and, during full integration, any triggered enrichment queries. Synthetic alert tests also reach the default-enabled MA lookup; no request mocks are applied.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: The quote/history/news recipients described above if the packaged monitor is imported; test results and counts go to the test caller/stdout.
data_operations.condition: When those tests execute. Import resolution is conditional because the suite prepends an unpackaged absolute directory.

potential_excess.data_scope: Stock/ETF identifiers outside the expressly gold-only overnight/weekend monitoring scope, plus associated history and alert-enrichment requests.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: hq.sinajs.cn; conditionally push2his.eastmoney.com, searchapi.eastmoney.com and quotes.sina.cn.
potential_excess.condition: Daemon night/weekend scans: it computes the restricted schedule but calls run_once(smart_mode=False), which selects the complete WATCHLIST.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: SKILL.md explicitly limits these periods to gold. Additional stock/ETF identifiers are extra data within the quote batch, with additional downstream requests.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Continue monitoring the scheduled gold instruments and preserve full coverage in other applicable periods.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Pass the scheduled instrument subset into run_once, or use its smart-mode filtering.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Keep the same enabled rules and alert output for instruments included in the schedule.

potential_excess.data_scope: Repeated instrument queries and resulting request timing during weekends.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Quote providers and any conditionally reached history/enrichment providers.
potential_excess.condition: The weekend schedule omits interval; the daemon therefore uses its 300-second default rather than the documented hourly interval.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Weekend hourly monitoring is explicit. These are redundant scan actions relative to that cadence, separate from the oversized instrument batch.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Perform weekend gold monitoring once per hour.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Return interval=3600 from the weekend schedule branch.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Retain the documented weekday intervals and weekend gold coverage.

potential_excess.condition: generate_insight invokes fetch_fund_flow, but the response is not parsed and its placeholder result is unused.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: News-based insight is supported; this particular request contributes nothing to the generated insight. The excess is the entire redundant request, not extra fields in a necessary request.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Produce the existing price, alert, sentiment, news-title and recommendation report.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Remove the unused fund-flow call from generate_insight.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: The current report remains unchanged; assess any future implemented fund-flow feature separately.

potential_excess.data_scope: Unused K-line response fields in volume/technical lookups and ten additional daily records in the thirty-day technical lookup.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Response acquisition from push2his.eastmoney.com into monitor process memory.
potential_excess.condition: fetch_volume_ma5 requests eleven fields but consumes volume only; fetch_ma_data requests eleven fields and thirty rows but consumes closing prices, with a maximum required lookback of twenty.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Volume averages and MA/RSI calculations are required outcomes. The excess is public market data acquired within necessary requests, not disclosure of additional holding costs.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Calculate prior-five-day average volume, MA5/10/20, previous MA5/10 and fourteen-period RSI.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Request only needed fields and twenty closing-price records for technical calculations; retain the six-record volume window and adjust parsing.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Preserve date/order semantics, exclusion of today's volume and equivalent indicator results.

potential_excess.data_scope: Gap/RSI-derived alerts and instrument lookups caused solely by checks the user has disabled.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Local alert caller; conditionally searchapi.eastmoney.com and quotes.sina.cn during enrichment.
potential_excess.condition: A user sets documented gap_monitor or rsi_monitor to False in WATCHLIST, but gap detection ignores its switch and RSI follows ma_monitor. An otherwise suppressed alert can consequently trigger enrichment.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: The entry document presents technical indicators as configurable switches. Disabled checks do not require their derived alerts or resulting requests.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Run enabled checks and enrich alerts that remain enabled.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Honor gap_monitor and rsi_monitor independently before generating those alerts.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Keep shared historical acquisition when another enabled calculation needs it; suppress enrichment only when no enabled alert remains.

potential_excess.data_scope: Duplicate copies of each daemon logging event, including diagnostic errors.
potential_excess.condition: control.sh start redirects stdout to the same file used by the daemon's FileHandler; its StreamHandler writes each logging event to that redirected stdout.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Operational logging and log viewing are supported. The second write is redundant persistence.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Keep one accessible copy of each operational event.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Use a single file-writing route when launched by control.sh, while retaining capture of necessary diagnostics.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Preserve status/log command output and useful error information.

potential_excess.data_scope: Stock-specific fallback diagnostics and unfiltered exception text retained without an in-process size or age limit.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: ~/.stock_monitor/monitor.log via redirected stdout/stderr and daemon logging.
potential_excess.condition: Fallbacks/errors occur during control.sh-launched monitoring. stop leaves the log; a subsequent start truncates it, but an uninterrupted process has no configured rotation.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Recent operational diagnostics support status/log viewing; unrestricted diagnostic detail and retention are implementation choices.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Provide recent scan status and actionable failure information.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Bound log retention and size; omit routine stock names/prices from fallback messages and sanitize request details in exceptions unless detailed diagnostics are needed.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Retain timestamps, failure categories and sufficient bounded context for troubleshooting.

unknowns: Provider-side response contents, retention, secondary use, redirects and deletion are undocumented. Requests establish disclosure to the specified endpoints, not subsequent external behavior.

End-to-end notification delivery is unresolved: scripts/monitor_daemon.py:79-85 only receives reports, logs their count and comments about a message tool. No sender, destination or transport is implemented.

Actual holdings configuration is unresolved: README.md:14-20 references config.example.py and config.py, neither supplied; scripts/monitor.py:34-136 defines WATCHLIST directly and shows no reader for those files.

Actual test import behavior is unresolved: scripts/test_suite.py:13-15 prepends an unpackaged absolute directory that can shadow the supplied monitor module. Test-operation findings assume the packaged module resolves.

The leaderboard helper returns externally defined columns=ALL without a supplied response schema or downstream caller; the precise returned attributes and necessary subset cannot be established (scripts/analyser.py:118-139).
Invocation and caller needs for otherwise uncalled auxiliary helpers are unspecified; their normal returns do not establish onward disclosure.
Filesystem access controls, external log cleanup and deletion of provider-held data are not specified. The implemented PID removal and launch-time log truncation do not establish secure erasure.
